draft.shortGloss: to stand; to be located; to say (text)
notes: Irregular verb: stond, stonden, heeft gestaan.
Dutch uses 'staan' for objects that rest upright or on a base (cars, furniture, buildings, glasses), where English simply uses 'to be'.

senses.definition: To be in an upright position on your feet.

examples.text: Er zijn geen stoelen meer, dus we moeten staan.
examples.translation: There are no chairs left, so we have to stand.

senses.definition: Of an upright object or vehicle: to be located or placed somewhere.

examples.text: De auto staat voor de deur.
examples.translation: The car is parked in front of the door.
examples.emotion: casual and matter-of-fact, pointing something out

senses.definition: To be written, printed, or shown somewhere.

examples.text: Wat staat er in de brief?
examples.emotion: curious and eager to know the contents
